source.title: Identity Crisis: Memorization and Generalization under Extreme Overparameterization
source.authors: Chiyuan Zhang; Samy Bengio; Moritz Hardt; M. Mozer; Y. Singer

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies an extreme single-example identity-mapping task, not natural-label classification, random-label memorization, or the test-error gap in the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The reported identity-map and constant-map results concern regression on a single example and do not measure any listed version's behavior. They are recorded as findings about a related construct under fits_no_version. Figures 4 and 8–10 provide additional quantitative or visual results, but the text does not state their individual values.
record.test_reason: The study measures identity-mapping regression and constant-output memorization, rather than any version's specified behavior. Its architecture, width and optimizer comparisons do not measure classification generalization, random-label fitting or the other named effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: under identity-reconstruction training, architectures exhibit markedly different biases toward identity generalization and constant-output memorization. The authors also emphasize sensitivity to depth, kernel size, channel count, initialization and optimizer.
record.recipe_differences: Single-example identity-mapping regression; standard gradient descent with no weight decay, rather than natural-label classification and the claim versions' test-error measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture depth, convolution filter size, channel count, initialization scheme, optimizer, and training-image size are reported to affect the learned inductive bias.

fits_no_version.finding: Shallow CNNs approximate the identity mapping after single-example training; very deep CNNs tend toward a constant output, with intermediate depths often behaving like edge detectors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth changes the inductive bias of CNNs trained on single-example identity reconstruction.

fits_no_version.finding: Fully connected networks fail to reconstruct inputs far from the training example; with 60,000 MNIST training examples, their reconstruction still fails on other input patterns while CNNs learn the identity mapping.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Convolutional architectures can generalize identity reconstruction beyond the training distribution better than fully connected architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing a five-layer CNN from three to many channels improves identity reconstruction, whereas widening a twenty-layer CNN does not remove its constant-output bias.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefit of width for single-example identity reconstruction depends on network depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix I reports that different optimizers reach global minimizers with different predictions on unseen reconstruction inputs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects inductive bias in single-example identity reconstruction.

record.problems: The main study uses one training image and an identity-mapping regression task, so it does not establish results for natural-label classification. Many quantitative comparisons are presented in figures without their individual values stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Figure-only measurements for depth, image size, filter size, and channel count were not transcribed as rows because the text does not provide their individual values; cited prior-work findings were excluded.

untested.parts: Paired random-label and natural-label classification experiments, including training fit and held-out accuracy relative to chance.
Whether widening beyond the zero-training-error threshold continues to lower classification test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifier test error, the contribution of local connectivity, and the specified initialization comparisons.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance on classification or language benchmarks under the specified tuning regimes and remedies.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and whether recipe adaptations remove a held-out performance penalty.
Dropout effects on classifier test error, including training-set size, dropout strength and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Influence-defined memorization and the test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The row states indicate that neither measure determines a listed claim version; both reported reconstruction phenomena are observed in the study. Figure 5's classification probe assesses representations from reconstruction-trained CNNs and supplies no convolutional-versus-fully-connected classifier comparison for V3.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural labels.
Whether widening past the zero-training-error threshold lowers test error.
Classifier test-error comparisons between convolutional and fully connected networks.
Adaptive-optimizer versus SGD held-out performance on classification or language benchmarks.
Large-batch effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects on classifier test error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the training–test gap.
Effects of removing memorized training examples on test accuracy.

rows.subject: CNNs, depth up-to-5 layers (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on one MNIST example to minimize reconstruction error on the identity-mapping task.
rows.measure: Approximation of the identity function on test inputs
rows.value: learn a fairly accurate approximation to the identity function, with the exception of a few artifacts at the boundaries
rows.note: Related identity-map generalization result; not a natural-label classification test-error result.
rows.check: The reported identity-map approximation is accurately paraphrased, but cannot establish any listed version. Appendix A specifies SGD with momentum 0.9, rather than SGD without momentum; evaluation includes Fashion-MNIST and synthetic inputs as well as MNIST.

rows.subject: CNNs, very deep (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on one MNIST example to minimize reconstruction error on the identity-mapping task.
rows.measure: Bias toward the constant function rather than the identity function on test inputs
rows.value: very deep CNNs bias towards the constant function
rows.note: The text also says intermediate-depth CNNs correlate well with neither reference function.
rows.check: The constant-output bias is explicitly reported, but cannot establish any listed version. This is memorization of a reconstruction target, not random-label fitting or example-level memorization as defined in V8. Evaluation also includes non-MNIST inputs.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
